core/io/ocr.py - scanned-PDF -> PageWords bridge (local RapidOCR + cloud vision).

Why this module exists
----------------------
``pdf_to_pages`` reads a PDF's *text layer*. A scanned / photographed PO has no
text layer at all, so pdfplumber returns ~zero words and the whole recipe engine
starves. This module rebuilds an equivalent token stream from the page IMAGE, so
every downstream stage (fingerprint -> recipe -> parser -> xlsx) runs unchanged.

Two engines, in priority order (user's choice: local-first, cloud fallback):

1. **Local — RapidOCR (onnxruntime)**. Fully offline, no API cost, returns real
   pixel bounding boxes. This is the primary path.
2. **Cloud — a vision LLM (default ``glm-4.6v``)**. Used only when RapidOCR is
   unavailable (not installed / not bundled) or yields nothing. A vision model
   returns *text*, not boxes, so we ask for a fixed-width transcription and
   rebuild pseudo-coordinates from character columns.

Coordinate contract (critical)
------------------------------
pdfplumber emits ``x0/top/x1/bottom`` in PDF **points** with a top-left origin.
Every token produced here is converted into that SAME space (pixels are scaled
by ``page_width_pt / pixmap_width_px``). That is what lets the matrix parsers —
which align quantities to size columns purely by X position — work identically
on scanned and digital POs.

All heavy dependencies (pymupdf / rapidocr / onnxruntime / cv2) are imported
lazily inside functions, so importing this module stays free and application
startup is unaffected when no scan is ever processed.

Transcribe this purchase-order page as PLAIN TEXT.
Rules:
1. Preserve the original table layout using spaces so that columns stay vertically aligned (fixed-width / monospace style).
2. Keep every number, code and label exactly as printed. Do not translate, reformat, round or reorder anything.
3. One physical line of the page = one line of output.
4. Output ONLY the transcription. No markdown, no code fences, no comments.

True when ``pages`` look like a scan (no usable text layer).

    Conservative by design: returns True only when the average word count per
    page falls under :data:`SPARSE_WORDS_PER_PAGE`, so a normal digital PO is
    never diverted into the (slower, lossier) OCR path.

Render pages with pdfium.

    Chosen over PyMuPDF because ``pypdfium2`` (6.9MB) is ALREADY bundled -
    pdfplumber depends on it for ``Page.to_image()`` - whereas PyMuPDF adds a
    further 37.7MB (mupdfcpp64.dll + _mupdf.pyd) to the installer for exactly
    the same "PDF page -> bitmap" job.
Legacy renderer - only used when pypdfium2 is somehow unavailable.

Render every page to PNG bytes.

    Returns a list of ``(page_index, png_bytes, width_pt, height_pt, scale)``
    where ``scale`` converts pixels -> PDF points.
OCR 需要 pypdfium2（随 pdfplumber 安装）或 PyMuPDF 来渲染页面。

Split one OCR *line* box into word tokens with interpolated X spans.

    OCR engines return a box per text line, but the parsers need word-level
    tokens (a matrix row's quantities must each carry their own X). We therefore
    distribute the line's width across its characters and slice each word out at
    its character offset — accurate enough to keep tabular columns aligned.

Force tokens on the same visual row to share one Y.

    ``PageWords.lines()`` groups by a fixed 3pt y-tolerance. Raw OCR boxes for
    the same printed row can drift several points apart (different columns are
    detected as separate boxes), which would shatter one row into several lines
    and break every grid parser. Clustering here and rewriting each cluster to
    its mean Y makes the downstream grouping deterministic.

Return the RapidOCR asset paths that are absent, or [] when all present.

    RapidOCR resolves ``config.yaml`` and ``models/*.onnx`` purely from
    ``Path(__file__).parent`` of its own package, so in a frozen build the
    files MUST be collected into ``_internal/rapidocr_onnxruntime/``. If the
    spec ever loses that ``collect_data_files`` entry the constructor blows up
    deep inside onnxruntime with an opaque error -- we check up front instead.

    NOTE: passing ``det_model_path=...`` kwargs is NOT a workaround: RapidOCR
    1.4.4's ``UpdateParameters.__call__`` builds ``new_config`` from the kwargs
    and then immediately overwrites it with ``update_global_to_module(config)``,
    so every path kwarg is silently discarded. Bundling is the only route.
True when RapidOCR + onnxruntime import AND its model files are present.
RapidOCR 模型文件缺失（打包遗漏）:
Run RapidOCR on one rendered page; return points-space PageWords.

Rebuild pseudo-coordinates from a fixed-width transcription.

    A vision model gives us characters, not boxes. Assuming the transcription
    keeps columns space-aligned (which the prompt demands), a word's character
    offset is a faithful proxy for its X position, and its line index for Y.
Transcribe one page with a vision LLM and rebuild PageWords.
云端 OCR 需要在线模型配置（base_url / api_key）
未配置 vision_model，无法使用云端 OCR 兜底

OCR every page of ``path`` -> PageWords in pdfplumber's coordinate space.

    Tries RapidOCR locally first; falls back to the configured cloud vision
    model per page when the local engine is missing or returns nothing. Pages
    that both engines fail on come back empty rather than raising, so one bad
    page cannot abort a multi-page document.
